text: Every climber at Scaffold Peaks has heard the story of the Ninth Rung. Halfway up the oldest ladder on the island, the story goes, one rung is colder than all the others, and anyone who stops there will hear music. Some say the music is a ghost; others say it is only the wind. Last winter, Indi decided to test the legend for herself. She climbed the ladder at dusk with Zed, a thermos of soup and a notebook full of questions. Sure enough, the ninth rung was icy to the touch, even through her gloves. When she paused there, a faint, tinkling tune drifted up from somewhere beneath them. Zed, who was two rungs below, swore he could hear nothing but the wind. Indi climbed back down, following the sound, until she found a narrow crack in the rock beside the ladder. Wedged deep inside was a tiny music box, its lid rusted half open. Somebody must have dropped it decades ago. Every time the wind blew across the crack, the little cylinder inside turned and played a few notes. Indi left the box exactly where it was. She told nobody except Zed, and Zed promised to keep quiet. Some legends, she decided, deserve to keep going.
